Due to severe injuries the petitioner has lost her entire future in her young age.
The petitioner is suffering with permanent disability.
She is not able to lead a normal life as prior to the accident.
4. It is the further case of the petitioner that, prior to the accident, the petitioner was hale and healthy, studying in BA Final year and she was very active and brilliant student.
Due to the accidental injuries, he became permanently disabled and could not concentrate on her studies.
She is fully depending on others.
The petitioner and their family members are in great hardship and mental agony.
5. The accident took place within the jurisdiction of Thuruvekere Traffic Police under Cr.No.4/2024 against the driver of the Car bearing Reg.No.KA-02-MD-7102.

Hence, the respondent Nos.1 & 2 being the RC Owner and the insurer of the Car bearing Reg.No.KA-02-MD-7102 and the Respondent Nos.3 & 4 being the Insurer and the RC owner of the motorcycle bearing No.KA-44-W-3170 are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner.

If so.

Issue No.1:

12. The chief examination of the PW.1 is nothing but a repetition of plaint averments.

The relevant portion of the PW.1 is herewith reproduced:
The PW.1 has deposed that: there was involvement of Two motorcycle and a Car in the accident.

14. It is well settled position of law that the proceedings under Motor Vehicle Act are summary in nature and it is beneficial legislation and the evidence required about negligence act is sufficient if it is in the nature of preponderance of probability.

As per Ex.P.7/Wound Certificate, the petitioner sustained injuries in a RTA on 06.01.2024 at about 4.00pm to 06.24pm, near Mayasandra, Aadichunchanagiri, Bellur, Nelamanagala, Mandya (D).

sentences.text: Therefore, on overall perusal of police documents, it is clear that the accident was occurred on 06.01.2024 and the petitioner sustained injuries as mentioned in Ex.P.7.
The point of dispute between the Exs.P.1 & 9 is that there was also negligence of the part of the rider of the motorcycle.
In deed, the driver of the Car has driven in a NH-150(a)/highway.
The materials on record clearly depicts that the said vehicle was coming from Mayasandra towards Bangalore and it was 30 feet road.

On careful scrutiny of evidence of the PW.2 and materials on records, it is clinches that the accident was occurred on the middle of the road and also there was sufficient space on the left side of the two wheeler viz., ridden by the rider of the petitioner's bike.
When such being the case, the rider of the bike can take their bike little left side to avoid accident.

In deed the police have filed the charge sheet against the driver of the offending car but the materials on record are clearly goes to show that the rider of the bike has also contributed to accident in question.
The mahazar clearly depicts that no break marks or blood stain marks in the incident place and it was high way NH-150A, 18ft. road.
So, the rider of the petitioner's bike was also rode the bike in a rashness manner and he failed to control the vehicle.

However, from the admissions of PW.1 and the sketch at Ex.P.3, it is clear that the major part of negligence for the accident was on the part of the driver of the Car since he was in high speed, driven the car in a rash and negligent manner.
It appears from the evidence of RW.1 that there were Three vehicles involved in the accident and it was head on collision.
Hence the Tribunal fixes the negligence at 70% on the part of the Car driver.
In the same manner the rider of the motorcycle would have not taken care of oncoming vehicle while riding his motorcycle.
Therefore, there is negligence on the part of the rider of the motorcycle also and the same is fixed at 30%.
Accordingly, issue No.1 is held partly in the affirmative.

she also complained of pain during menstruation, both hip movements were restricted and X-ray pelvis with both hips AP view showed healed fracture of right side superior and inferior pubic rami facture with pubic symphysis diastasis persisting.

17. Before discussing on this point, it is necessary to advert to the observations made by the Raj Kumar vs. Ajay Kumar.

The Hon'ble Supreme Court has held that, "the provision of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 makes it clear that the award must be just, which means that compensation should, to the extent possible, fully and adequately restore the claimant to the position prior to the accident.
The object of awarding damages is to make good the loss suffered as a result of wrong done as far as money can do so, in a fair, reasonable and equitable manner.

The Court or Tribunal shall have to assess the damages objectively and exclude from consideration any speculation or 1 2011 ACJ 1 fancy, though some conjecture with reference to the nature of disability and its consequences,
is inevitable.
A person is not only to be compensated for the physical injury, but also for the loss which he suffered as a result of such injury.

This means that he is to be compensated for his inability to lead a full life, his inability to enjoy those normal amenities which he would have enjoyed but for the injuries, and his inability to earn as much as he used to earn or could have earned".
18.

Our Hon'ble High Court has held in a case MFA.811 OF 2015 (MV-I) decided on 18 July, 2019 in between Rajanna @ Raju and another V/s Srinivas and another that "It is necessary to understand the meaning of the expression "permanent disability", which has been elucidated in Rajkumar.

entities.text: Rajanna @ Raju and another V/s Srinivas and another
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: According to the Hon'ble Supreme Court, disability refers to any restriction or lack of ability to perform an activity in the manner considered normal for a human being.

Permanent disability refers to the residuary incapacity or loss of use of some part of the body, found existing at the end of the period of treatment and recuperation, after achieving the maximum bodily improvement or recovery which is likely to remain for the remainder life of the injured.
Temporary disability refers to the incapacity or loss of use of some part of the body on account of the injury, which will cease to exist at the end of the period of treatment and recuperation.
Permanent disability can be either partial or total.

Partial permanent disability refers to a person's inability to perform all the duties and bodily functions that he could perform before the accident, though he is able to perform some of them and is still able to engage in some gainful activity.
Total permanent disability refers to a person's inability to perform any avocation or employment related activities as a result of the accident.

The permanent disabilities that may arise from motor accidents injuries, are of a much wider range when compared to the physical disabilities which are enumerated in the Persons with Disabilities (Equal Opportunities, Protection of Rights and Full Participation) Act, 1995 ("the Disabilities Act",
for short).

entities.text: Persons with Disabilities (Equal Opportunities, Protection of Rights and Full Participation) Act, 1995
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: But if any of the disabilities enumerated in Section 2(i) of the Disabilities Act are the result of injuries sustained in a motor accident, they can be permanent disabilities for the purpose of claiming compensation.

12. Therefore, the Tribunal has to first decide whether there is any permanent disability and, if so,
the extent of such permanent disability.

sentences.text: By considering the dictums of Hon'ble Supreme Court and Our Hon'ble High Court and also evidence led by the medical officer, It is appears to Court that, the petitioner has sustained grievous injuries.
And it certainly affected on functioning over the hearing, left facial movement, movement of teeth and chewing.
The medical officer has given permanent physical disability at 53.56 Points and to the whole body at 17.85%.
The petition discloses that the petitioner was a student studying final year Degree.
The evidence of the medical officer clearly clinches that there is no problem for reading and writing.
It means, the petitioner can do her day today work as earlier with some difficulty.
As such, the petitioner has suffered permanent disability of 15% whole body.

the claimant is entitled for the compensation under the following heads.
PECUNIARY DAMAGES I.

Expenses relating to treatment, hospitalization, medicines,
transportation, nourishing food and misc. expenditures.

sentences.text: The documents placed by the petitioner indicates that she has taken treatment before the said hospitals.
Further the Discharge Summaries at Ex.P.6 produced by the PW.1 indicates that, the petitioner was admitted on 07.01.2024 and discharged on 17.01.2024 at Sanjay Gandhi Hospital, Bangalore.
The petitioner has produced the medical/cash bill for Rs.42,637/-.
On careful perusal of the medical bills, it is appears to Court that there is no repetitive bills, advance bills.
There is no contrary evidence from the respondents.
Hence, I award a sum of Rs.42,637/- as compensation to the claimant under the head of treatment and medical expenses.
As supra said, the petitioner has admitted in the said Hospitals as inpatient for a period of nearly 12 days.
Hence, it is just and proper to award a sum of Rs.500/-per day for attendant and Rs.500/- for food and nourishment charges, which would comes Rs.12,000/-.
A sum of Rs.12,000/- is awarded under the head of attendant, food and nourishment charges.

(b) LOSS OF FUTURE EARNING ON ACCOUNT OF PERMANENT DISABILITY:
22.
The claimant has examined the Doctor to substantiate the disability as PW-2.
As already discussed above, the petitioner was suffered disability of 15%.
The PW.2 has opined that the petitioner has disability of 15% Points for functional loss of malocclusion.
As per the petition averments, the age of the claimant is 21 years.
The Aadhar Card marked at Ex.P10 clearly discloses that, the age of the petitioner was 20 years.
Therefore, the age of the claimant is considered as 20 years to assess the loss of future earning and the multiplier is 18.
As I have already stated the notional income of the claimant is Rs.16,500/-pm.
The loss of future earning is calculated as Rs.16,500/- (Monthly income X 12 (Months) X 18 X 15%/100 = Rs.5,34,600/- which is the just and proper compensation payable to claimant.
NON PECUNIARY DAMAGES (GENERAL DAMAGES)

Permanent disability refers to the residuary incapacity or loss of use of some part of the body, found existing at the end of the period of treatment and recuperation, after achieving the maximum bodily improvement or recovery which is likely to remain for the remainder life of the injured.
Temporary disability refers to the incapacity or loss of use of some part of the body on account of the injury, which will cease to exist at the end of the period of treatment and recuperation.
Permanent disability can be either partial or total.
Partial permanent disability refers to a person's inability to perform all the duties and bodily functions that he could perform before the accident, though he is able to perform some of them and is still able to engage in some gainful activity.
Total permanent disability refers to a person's inability to perform any avocation or employment related activities as a result of the accident.
The permanent disabilities that may arise from motor accidents injuries, are of a much wider range when compared to the physical disabilities which are enumerated in the Persons with Disabilities (Equal Opportunities, Protection of Rights and Full Participation) Act, 1995 ("the Disabilities Act",
for short).
But if any of the disabilities enumerated in Section 2(i) of the Disabilities Act are the result of injuries sustained in a motor accident, they can be permanent disabilities for the purpose of claiming compensation.
